referee_caveats_inferred: Dust mass depends on assumed kappa (2.3 cm2/g, from a 1990 work) and on a luminosity-based temperature with an arbitrary 50/50 split; the optically thick asymmetry the authors argue for undermines the optically thin mass assumption
Inclination from arccos(b/a) of a Gaussian ignores the geometric thickness the authors claim, so inclinations and SLAM masses (sin^2 i) are biased
SLAM masses differ strongly between ridge and edge (A: 0.5 vs 0.91 Msun) with errors up to 100%, and fitted p of 0.35 for disk A is far from Keplerian, so Keplerian rotation is not firmly shown
Fitted systemic velocities (5.05 and 4.87 vs 5.48 and 5.46 km/s) differ from the adopted 5.86 km/s, suggesting contamination or an offset the paper does not resolve
Numbers differ between abstract/text and conclusions (dust masses 22.5/12.4 vs 21.9/12.7; 53.0 vs 52.0; disk radius quoted 180 mas versus 26.9 au; disk B p ridge 0.43 vs 0.4)
Outflow dynamical age (~280 yr) uses a visually chosen maximum velocity and a single inclination
No radiative-transfer model supports the near/far-side asymmetry or over-subtraction explanation; no substructure search beyond Gaussian residual inspection
